title: Aperture
basic_theory: Aperture is the opening inside the lens.
points: A small f-number, such as f/2.8 or f/4, means a wider opening.
A wide opening allows more light and can produce a blurrier background.
A larger f-number, such as f/8 or f/11, means a narrower opening.
A narrow opening allows less light and can keep more of the scene in focus.
teaching_prompt: Do you want one subject to stand out, or do you want the whole scene to feel important?
caution: Avoid relying only on the phrases “large aperture” and “small aperture,” which can confuse beginners. Say “wide opening / small f-number” and “narrow opening / large f-number.”
